scenes.visual: Title card: A Second Place to Double.

scenes.tts: Human neurogenesis lasts months, not the mouse's week. Where might extra divisions happen? And why wouldn't they simply make our cortex thick?
scenes.visual: A timeline: mouse, about a week; human, months. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Human neurogenesis lasts months, not the mouse's week. Where might extra divisions happen? And why wouldn't they simply make our cortex thick?

scenes.tts: Rakic built his model around progenitors at the ventricle. But in fetal monkey cortex, the zone above them is split in two.
scenes.visual: The cortical wall labelled from the bottom: ventricular zone, inner subventricular zone, outer subventricular zone.
scenes.narration: Rakic built his model around progenitors at the ventricle. But in fetal monkey cortex, the zone above them is split in two.

scenes.tts: What was dividing in the outer part?
scenes.visual: The outer subventricular zone highlighted with a question mark.
scenes.narration: What was dividing in the outer part?

scenes.tts: In two thousand ten, Hansen, Kriegstein and colleagues filmed living slices of human fetal cortex.
scenes.caption: In 2010, Hansen, Kriegstein and colleagues filmed living slices of human fetal cortex.
scenes.visual: Name card: Hansen, Lui, Parker and Kriegstein, 2010. A slice of fetal cortex under a microscope.
scenes.narration: In 2010, Hansen, Kriegstein and colleagues filmed living slices of human fetal cortex.

scenes.tts: They found cells with the markers of radial glia, the proteins pax six and sox two.
scenes.caption: They found cells with the markers of radial glia, the proteins PAX6 and SOX2.
scenes.visual: A cell in the outer zone glowing, labelled PAX6 and SOX2.
scenes.narration: They found cells with the markers of radial glia, the proteins PAX6 and SOX2.

scenes.tts: These cells kept a fibre toward the brain surface, but had no process touching the ventricle.
scenes.visual: The cell drawn with a basal fibre running up to the surface and no process reaching the ventricle.
scenes.narration: These cells kept a fibre toward the brain surface, but had no process touching the ventricle.

scenes.tts: Before dividing, a cell moved its cell body up its fibre. Daughters could divide again, or become intermediate progenitors, which soon make neurons.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse style: the cell body slides up the fibre, a dashed outline marking where it was, then divides. One daughter keeps the fibre; the other is labelled intermediate progenitor, TBR2.
scenes.narration: Before dividing, a cell moved its cell body up its fibre. Daughters could divide again, or become intermediate progenitors, which soon make neurons.

scenes.tts: These are outer radial glia. Later imaging in fetal macaque found them making proliferative divisions too.
scenes.visual: Label: outer radial glia. Name card: Betizeau and colleagues, 2013, macaque. One cell divides into two progenitors.
scenes.narration: These are outer radial glia. Later imaging in fetal macaque found them making proliferative divisions too.

scenes.tts: So, in macaque at least, they can be a second site of doubling.
scenes.visual: Two sites marked: founders at the ventricle; outer radial glia in the outer zone. Label: second site of doubling seen in macaque.
scenes.narration: So, in macaque at least, they can be a second site of doubling.

scenes.tts: How much can a little doubling matter? Take a toy lineage. One progenitor divides for sixty rounds, and each division adds a neuron.
scenes.caption: How much can a little doubling matter? Take a toy lineage. One progenitor divides for 60 rounds, and each division adds a neuron.
scenes.visual: Card: toy lineage, not a measurement. A single line of 60 rounds, one neuron dropping off each time.
scenes.narration: How much can a little doubling matter? Take a toy lineage. One progenitor divides for 60 rounds, and each division adds a neuron.

scenes.tts: That makes sixty neurons.
scenes.caption: That makes 60 neurons.
scenes.visual: On screen: 60 divisions, all adding: 60 neurons.
scenes.narration: That makes 60 neurons.

scenes.tts: Predict. Now, in every round, give each progenitor a one in ten chance of making two progenitors instead.
scenes.visual: On screen: each round, each progenitor has a 1 in 10 chance of making two progenitors, otherwise a progenitor and a neuron. No cell stops or dies.
scenes.narration: Predict. Now, in every round, give each progenitor a one in ten chance of making two progenitors instead.

scenes.tts: Every progenitor keeps dividing. On average, do you get about sixty neurons, a few hundred, or thousands?
scenes.caption: Every progenitor keeps dividing. On average, do you get about 60 neurons, a few hundred, or thousands?
scenes.visual: Three choices: about 60; a few hundred; thousands. Label: on average.
scenes.narration: Every progenitor keeps dividing. On average, do you get about 60 neurons, a few hundred, or thousands?

scenes.visual: Choices held.

scenes.tts: Thousands, on average. Each doubling adds a progenitor that keeps dividing, so the pool grows by a tenth each round, like compound interest.
scenes.visual: On screen: expected neurons = 9 × (1.1⁶⁰ − 1), about 2,700; about 300 progenitors still cycling. The lineage tree branches and widens over time.
scenes.narration: Thousands, on average. Each doubling adds a progenitor that keeps dividing, so the pool grows by a tenth each round, like compound interest.

scenes.tts: Given enough rounds, a little doubling outgrows a lot of adding.
scenes.visual: Caption: given enough rounds, a little doubling outgrows a lot of adding.
scenes.narration: Given enough rounds, a little doubling outgrows a lot of adding.

scenes.visual: The wide lineage tree held.

scenes.tts: So why no thicker cortex? Predict. New neurons climb radial glial fibres. If every fibre ran straight up, with packing fixed, what would extra neurons do?
scenes.visual: Parallel straight fibres rising from the outer zone. Label: cartoon, surface and packing fixed. Question card.
scenes.narration: So why no thicker cortex? Predict. New neurons climb radial glial fibres. If every fibre ran straight up, with packing fixed, what would extra neurons do?

scenes.visual: Question card held.

scenes.tts: In this cartoon, they would stack onto existing columns, and the cortex would thicken.
scenes.visual: Neurons pile up on straight fibres; the columns grow taller.
scenes.narration: In this cartoon, they would stack onto existing columns, and the cortex would thicken.

scenes.tts: Instead, the fibres diverge as they climb, fanning the scaffold outward. That favours spreading the neurons sideways, into area.
scenes.visual: The fibres redrawn diverging in a fan toward the surface; neurons spread across it and the surface lengthens. Label: favours area.
scenes.narration: Instead, the fibres diverge as they climb, fanning the scaffold outward. That favours spreading the neurons sideways, into area.

scenes.visual: The fan held.

scenes.tts: Outer radial glia are not uniquely human. Mice have a few, and ferrets and primates have many.
scenes.visual: Species strip: mouse (few cells), ferret (many), macaque (many), human (many).
scenes.narration: Outer radial glia are not uniquely human. Mice have a few, and ferrets and primates have many.

scenes.tts: The human outer subventricular zone is especially large.
scenes.visual: The human outer zone drawn largest.
scenes.narration: The human outer subventricular zone is especially large.

scenes.tts: The marmoset, whose cortex is nearly smooth, has them too. So they are not enough for folding on their own.
scenes.visual: Marmoset added: outer radial glia present, smooth cortex. Label: not enough for folding alone.
scenes.narration: The marmoset, whose cortex is nearly smooth, has them too. So they are not enough for folding on their own.

scenes.tts: Founders can double at the ventricle. Outer radial glia can double far from it, and their fanned fibres favour area over thickness.
scenes.visual: Closing card: two places to double; fanned fibres favour area.
scenes.narration: Founders can double at the ventricle. Outer radial glia can double far from it, and their fanned fibres favour area over thickness.

scenes.visual: Closing card held.
